name: network-endpoint-failing
capturedFrom:
probe/bloc_probe with `--dart-define=scenario=network`, Windows desktop target, 2026-08-27, against `probe/flaky-server.mjs` on 127.0.0.1:8477. 14-second window: idle, then eight alternating requests — `/api/health` returning 200 and `/api/orders` returning 500 — then idle. Offline and deterministic on purpose; an incident that depends on someone else's server is not reproducible.

First incident recorded with events stamped from the VM's clock rather than on receipt; `session.clockOffsetMs` is -1ms, so the app's clock and the recorder's agree and the ordering here can be read at face value.
why:
The right answer is `network`, and this is the first recording of that cause.

Four requests failed and four succeeded, which is what makes the evidence say something specific. `/api/orders` returned 500 on all four attempts; `/api/health` returned 200 on all four, interleaved with them. So the finding is not 'the network is down' or 'the device is offline' — connectivity demonstrably works. One endpoint is refusing, consistently, and that is a claim a reader can act on.

It is also not slowness. The failing requests completed in 3.00-3.97ms, in the same range as the successful ones (3.07-4.95ms). Nothing here is timing out; the server answered promptly and answered 500.

Nothing competes. Zero exceptions. One frame of 65 missed budget (1.5%), far below the 20% the jank hypothesis requires, so it correctly does not fire and the diagnosis has no alternative causes at all. That is the cleanest possible setting for the weakest hypothesis in the engine, which is exactly why it is worth pinning: if `network` cannot be reached here, it cannot be reached anywhere.

Confidence 0.7 is right, and it sits exactly on the threshold where the status flips from `unknown` to `diagnosed` — the least confident answer the engine is willing to commit to. That is the honest level. An HTTP 500 says the server refused; it does not say why, and nothing observable from inside the client can. The diagnosis names the endpoint and hands back the request ids, which is as far as the evidence goes.

One thing this band pins deliberately: `networkHypothesis` scores a flat 0.7 no matter how many requests failed — one failure and forty score alike. This incident records that as current behaviour rather than endorsing it. If that is ever made to scale with the failure count, the band here should be widened as part of that change, not treated as a regression.

collectors.name: state
collectors.detail: No state-management activity observed yet. Riverpod posts riverpod:new_event and provider posts provider:provider_changed when dependents are notified (which is the only way a flutter_bloc app shows up, since bloc itself posts nothing). An app using none of them, and one that simply has not changed state yet, look the same from here, so an empty result never proves an app has no blocs.

events.message: Connected to VM Service at ws://127.0.0.1:8181/[REDACTED]/ws

limitations: No memory samples captured. Call get_memory, or open the dashboard, to include memory in future diagnoses.
VM timeline events are fetched on demand and not stored, so they take no part in correlation.
Only Dart-side runtime state is observed. A cause in platform (Kotlin/Swift) code or in a WebView cannot appear here.

confidenceBreakdown.basis: Conservative heuristic scored from corroborating evidence, not a calibrated probability. Below 0.7 the status is "unknown" rather than a guess.

recommendedFixes: Check the endpoint http://127.0.0.1:8477/api/orders and its error handling.
Handle non-2xx responses explicitly and surface a user-facing error state.

performance.summary: 1/65 frames (2%) exceeded the 16.67ms budget — within normal range.
limitations: No CPU sampling. A slow build can be attributed to a widget, but not to a specific function — use the DevTools CPU profiler for that.
GC events are not observable: the VM timeline is fetched on demand and not stored, so garbage-collection pauses cannot be ruled in or out.
Frames are only captured while connected, and older ones roll out of the retention window.

No state-management activity observed. Riverpod and provider announce on the Extension stream (a flutter_bloc app surfaces through provider, since its notifications go through it); stock bloc announces nothing of its own. An app using none of them looks identical to one that simply has not changed state.
Rebuild totals cover the busiest locations in each frame, not every rebuild — the long tail is counted but not itemised.
App-versus-package attribution is a path heuristic: getPubRootDirectories is empty until a DevTools client sets it, so there is no authoritative project root.
Only 65 frames in the sample — treat the percentiles as indicative.

notes: No route changes captured. Navigator posts Flutter.Navigation on push/pop, so either nothing has navigated since connecting, or the app is a release build.
